transcript.dialogue: Hi Dex, I'm Mira. Careful with that handshake, I think my fingers are still mostly ink.
Nice to meet you, Mira. Ink's better than what's on my hands usually. That's just mud and old kiln dust. What kind of work needs your fingers that stained?
I make maps, mostly of places that tend to shift around when you aren't looking. What about the kiln dust? Are you building things that stay put?
Mostly just planters and mugs, things that don't go anywhere once they're fired. How do you map a place that moves?
transcript.action: tap scarred knuckles on the table

transcript.dialogue: You use a lot of baseline coordinates, I use a lot of hope. Let's just say my cartography is mostly fictional, like Tuesdays.
Well, Tuesdays can certainly drag cartographically. I used to measure time by how many times I was allowed to wear the fireproof Nomex suit before it smelled like a campfire.
A campfire suit sounds like a heavy way to measure a Tuesday. Did you trade the fire for the kiln to keep things predictable?
Pretty much. Kilns don't surprise you if you watch the cones. It's nice just walking out into the cool air like this.
It really is. Let's walk before the rest of the chairs lock us in.
Lead the way, Mira. I've got two bad knees that appreciate a flat sidewalk after a long night on these tile floors.
transcript.action: stand up and head for the door

transcript.dialogue: Hi Nell, I'm Mira. Careful with that cardigan, my cuffs are still mostly ink from this afternoon.
Ink's fine. My pockets usually have spare index cards anyway, so it balances out.
Index cards are good. Do you file them by topic or just shove them in wherever they fit?
By topic. Usually chronological by century, though I've got a separate bundle for regional variations.
Oh. Right. Centuries. That's... a lot of filing. Honestly, Nell, I think I'm losing steam on the trivia thing.
I went too specific. Sorry. What kind of ink was on your cuffs?
Just drafting ink. Walnut, usually. It doesn't really wash out.
I can see yourself out, then. Have a good night, Mira.

transcript.dialogue: At least these two have the menu memorized, or they've rehearsed it since Tuesday. How are you holding up?
I survived worse than a rehearsed menu. But I wouldn't mind finding an exit before they start harmonizing.
Agreed. If they start trading matching sweaters, I'm diving out the window. How's your week been outside the studio?
Quiet enough. Just throwing small bowls mostly, and trying not to drop the heavy ones. How about your drawing table?
Oh, you know, just chasing lines that won't stay put. I'll pass on that after-party. Let's stay right here.
I can drink to staying right here. The studio's been just as quiet, thankfully. No fire today, just mud.
Mud sounds much better than whatever show outside just tried to cast us. How's your week been besides the clay?
Just more clay and a lot of quiet. I'd like to bring you some of those mugs I mentioned, maybe down by the river this Thursday if you're free.
Thursday sounds perfect. Let's meet by the old bridge and see where we end up.
Thursday by the old bridge sounds just right. Let's walk before it gets any colder.
